convoLines.text: «Não entendo nada. Nada!» "You good?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
They answer at length. They nod, holding your gaze a beat longer.
They answer at length. A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
They answer at length. You point at yourself, then at them, then at the fire. Together. They get it.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. Sounds, and the shape of meaning just out of reach.
Benjamin laughs — with you, mostly. "Good try! Again — Sim, sim, exato.." They walk you through it, patient as sunrise.
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"They'd tell me to keep working. So I'm working. That's the whole plan."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sure — what's on your mind? Just thinking out loud."
"Aki is gone and Aknur is gone. The fire doesn't care. That's what gets me — the fire doesn't care."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"I keep turning over the last thing Aknur said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Adaeze grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Adaeze is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"The fire feels smaller without Aknur. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"Still on what's been happening. Just an idea."
You show them Pawpaw — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
They speak. You understand none of it.
They answer at length. They nod back, a little quicker this time.
They answer at length. They smile back, slower this time, like it just landed.
They answer at length. You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
They spread their hands, smiling — the words are missing, but the meaning lands anyway.
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Right. Go on, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Never mind the pantry run — we got it handled. Thanks anyway. I hate to ask this, but I'm achy and wrung out, barely keeping food down. Will you help me?"
"I'm burning up and there's nothing left in me. Someone who knows sickness — please."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"I know you and Felicia were close. I'm sorry."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"I write everything down. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Adaeze nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Pawpaw — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

They spread their hands, smiling — the words are missing, but the meaning lands anyway.
"Yeah? What's up? ...sorry."
A gesture, patient and clear: palms up, then toward you.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They nod along, following your hands more than your words.
Their gestures slow — the conversation thinning like light at dusk.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Don't mind me. Today's just heavy."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
You walk to the cache spot with Maher. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"I — yeah. It helps, hearing that."
"Can you — would you stay close tonight? I don't want to be alone when it gets dark."
"I keep hearing things past the treeline. I know it's probably nothing. I just — don't want to be alone with it tonight."

lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Felicia Noh is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Felicia Noh is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Felicia kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Felicia's gone." Aki looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Felicia." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Eamon blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Brawler's Instinct (Level 1). You read a fight as it moves. The body tells you what the mouth won't.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Scrounger (Level 1). Ruin looting finds +1 item.

d41: The warm hum behind your ribs is gone. The reactor went with Felicia's body — it does not come out, and it does not pass on. Hunger is back on the table. (One reactor per world, and the world already spent its one.)
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Felicia Noh, 41 days. The mantle passes to Eamon Ricci.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Eamon Ricci, 57 — a dockworker. His hands know different work now: Beast-calm, Adrenaline Control.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Felicia — and Felicia is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: You knew Felicia — not the office, the person. The fire keeps expecting them, and so do you. That's a heavier kind of stepping up. (+5 trauma)
d41: At the grave, Benjamin, Aki, Sari and 1 more speak for Eamon — "Felicia trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Eamon before the Codex did — his name already carried weight here.
